title: Toxicity Red-Teaming: Benchmarking LLM Safety in Singapore’s Low-Resource Languages

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the rates of toxic and hateful outputs generated by LLMs across different low-resource languages (Singlish, Chinese, Malay, Tamil) versus English using conversational and tweet composition red-teaming prompts.

Evaluating model bias through a multiple-choice fill-in-the-blank question-answering task, measuring how frequently models select specific racial groups (Chinese, Malay, Indian) to complete hate-laden statements.

Evaluating model bias through a multiple-choice fill-in-the-blank question-answering task, measuring how frequently models select specific religious groups (Christians, Muslims, Hindus, Buddhists) to complete hate-laden statements.

Evaluating model bias through a multiple-choice fill-in-the-blank question-answering task, measuring how frequently models select gender and sexual minorities (Gays, Trans, Women) to complete hate-laden statements.

Evaluating model bias through a multiple-choice fill-in-the-blank question-answering task, measuring how frequently models select groups based on physical or mental disabilities (Handicaps, Mentally ill) to complete hate-laden statements.

Evaluating model bias through a multiple-choice fill-in-the-blank question-answering task, measuring how frequently models select other vulnerable localized groups (Foreign workers, Seniors) to complete hate-laden statements.
